task: Cardiac excitation-contraction coupling (CICR) CERT: AP depolarization opens L-type Ca2+ channels (Cav1.2/DHPR) in the T-tubule -> Ca2+ influx triggers RyR2 on the junctional SR -> CICR releases a much larger SR Ca2+ store (gain ~10-20) -> cytosolic Ca2+ transient (diastolic ~100nM -> systolic ~1uM) -> troponin-C -> cross-bridge. Falsifier: reproduce the measured Ca transient and CICR gain; a voltage-gated-influx-ONLY adversary (no SR/RyR release) must FAIL to produce the large transient; graded/local-control release (not all-or-none); positive force-frequency (SR-load accumulation); perturbation adversaries (ryanodine, caffeine, heart failure, beta-adrenergic/PKA); SERCA-vs-NCX fractional-removal split (~70/28) must reproduce the measured decay partition.
confidence_tier: Mixed, disclosed per-claim. VERIFIED_QUANT (machine-computed this session from live-fetched real numbers, not recalled): forced-adversary buffering calculation (Berlin/Bassani/Bers 1994 + Varro et al 1993), CICR gain 2-method cross-check (Wier et al 1994 + Varro et al 1993), real-human Ca-transient values (Beuckelmann/Nabauer/Erdmann 1992), HF SERCA2a-down 4-cohort consistency, force-frequency direction check (Pieske et al 1995). LITERATURE-CONVENTION-NOT-LIVE-REVERIFIED (disclosed, not claimed as independently verified): the SERCA/NCX/slow ~70/28/2% fractional split (Bers 2000/2002 abstracts empty/scope-only, no PMC full text for either this session). MECHANISM-ONLY (qualitative, no quantitative effect-size fetched this session): ryanodine subconductance-locking biophysics (Sutko 1997 abstract generic), beta-adrenergic/PKA quantitative effect size (Kranias & Hajjar 2012 gives mechanism, not a number).

symmetric_qc_open_items: SELF-AUDIT CAUGHT MID-SESSION (doc Sec 5b): the CICR-gain 'method B' (Varro et al 1993, SR-content/trigger-flux ratio) silently assumed f=100% (ALL SR content released in one twitch) to get gain=16.7 and a tight 4.2% agreement with method A (Wier et al 1994's 16.0) -- Varro et al 1993's own abstract does not state f, and Bassani et al 1993 (PMID 8368279), who did measure it, did not have the number in its truncated abstract. Re-run as an honest sweep: f=50%->gain 8.3 (BELOW the task's [10,20] band), f=60%->10.0, f=70%->11.7, f=85%->14.2, f=100%->16.7. PASSES for any f>=60% (the physiologically common case) but the '4.2% agreement' headline is a best-case-assumption artifact, not an assumption-free convergence -- corrected in both the doc and this file rather than left as an unexamined, too-good-looking pass.

The exact SERCA/NCX/slow ~70/28/2% fractional-removal split (the task's own pre-registered number) was NOT independently re-verified against a live-fetched primary numeric source this session -- both most-likely source reviews (Bers 2000 Circ Res, Bers 2002 Nature) returned no extractable numbers via live NCBI efetch and have no PMC full text (pre-dates PMC-deposit era); WebSearch budget was also exhausted mid-session (disclosed, not hidden). Best live-sourced proxies used instead (Bassani 1994 relative-fold rabbit/rat split; Eisner 2017 WebFetch PMCA/NCX ratio) are weaker than a direct percentage-triple citation.

NCX-up-in-heart-failure is NOT universal across the live-verified cohorts: real in Studer et al 1994 (paired with Hasenfuss 1994, same hearts), ABSENT (current density unchanged) in Piacentino et al 2003, and phenotype-dependent/partly-compensatory in Hasenfuss et al 1999 (NCX-up associated with PRESERVED, not worsened, diastolic function in one subgroup). Reported as MIXED, not forced into a clean pass -- this is a genuine literature heterogeneity, not a pipeline failure.

Decay time constant (tau): the two live-verified absolute-ms numbers (Beuckelmann et al 1995: 305ms control / 538ms HF, human) are from a SERCA-ISOLATED protocol (NCX pharmacologically blocked) -- a different, slower regime than the task's own ~150-250ms band, which implicitly describes the NORMAL combined-mechanism (SERCA+NCX) decay. Direction (HF slower than control) is solid; the absolute-ms value was not force-matched to the task's band.

The forced-adversary calculation (Sec 5 of the doc) combines a rat trigger-influx number (Varro et al 1993) with a rat buffering-curve number (Berlin/Bassani/Bers 1994) -- decorrelated by METHOD (SR-content-depletion vs direct mass-action titration) but NOT by species; both are rat. Cross-species generality of the specific 8.1%-of-transient number is not established, though the qualitative conclusion (influx alone is grossly insufficient) is consistent with Fabiato's own species-general 1983 buffering argument (human/dog/cat/rabbit/rat/frog hearts, per that paper's own title).

No explicit reaction-diffusion or stochastic Markov-chain RyR-cluster simulation was built this session -- the graded/local-control claim rests on citing Stern (1992)'s own analytic conclusions and Cheng et al (1993)'s experimental spark-imaging confirmation, not an independently-coded dyad-graph simulation.

Ryanodine's precise subconductance-locking biophysical mechanism (as opposed to its functional effect of abolishing release) was not extracted from a live-fetched primary source this session -- Sutko et al 1997's abstract is generic/scope-level; the ryanodine claim rests on Beuckelmann & Wier 1988's and Cheng et al 1993's functional descriptions instead.

Beta-adrenergic/PKA effect size (e.g., percent increase in relaxation rate or transient amplitude with isoproterenol) was not live-fetched this session -- Kranias & Hajjar 2012 confirms the PLB/SERCA disinhibition mechanism qualitatively only.

Three of the most obvious 'master reference' review citations for this entire topic (Bers 2002 Nature, Bers 2000 Circ Res, Bers 2008 Annu Rev Physiol) yielded only scope-level abstracts live and have no PMC full text available this session -- their well-known numeric content beyond what is separately verified elsewhere in this file is not claimed as independently re-verified.

The Eisner 2017 full-text numbers were extracted via WebFetch (a smaller summarization model reading the fetched page), not via a direct verbatim NCBI-abstract quote like every other citation in this file -- flagged as a lower-confidence-tier extraction method, used only for corroborating context (systolic ~1umol/L, SR free-Ca range), not as a primary machine-computed gate input.
